questions.text:
QUESTION ONE: THE DOPPLER EFFECT

Tane and Kiri are riding their jet boats on a lake. Tane's boat has an air horn emitting 980 Hz. At one point, Kiri stops and Tane travels directly toward her at 24.5 m s-1. Speed of sound = 343 m s-1.

Calculate the frequency Kiri hears.
Explain why Kiri hears a different frequency than that emitted by the horn.
questions.expectedAnswer: As the boat approaches, wave fronts bunch up in front, making the apparent wavelength shorter. Since the speed of sound is constant, shorter wavelength means higher frequency.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- ONE point.

For Merit:
- Complete answer.

questions.text:
Kiri is floating close to Tane's path while her friend Moana watches from the bank. The graph below shows the frequency heard by each observer as the boat travels past.

Explain why the frequency Kiri hears is the same or different to that which Moana hears.
questions.expectedAnswer: When the boat is far away and approaching, both hear similar frequencies (nearly same component of velocity toward each). As it passes Kiri directly, she hears the actual frequency momentarily, then hears a much lower frequency (directly receding). Moana, offset from the path, always has a component of velocity toward/away from her that is less than the full speed, so her frequency change is more gradual and less extreme.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Explains one section.

For Merit:
- Explains transition.

For Excellence:
- Complete answer.

questions.text:
QUESTION TWO: STANDING WAVES

The guitar is a stringed instrument. The strings are supported at each end by the bridge and the nut. The length of the strings between the supports is 0.650 m. The strings vibrate in different harmonics.

Draw a diagram of the 3rd harmonic. Label nodes and antinodes.
questions.expectedAnswer: Diagram showing 3rd harmonic on a string fixed at both ends: 3 antinodes, 4 nodes.

questions.text:
If the guitar has been in storage, the tension may decrease. Use the equation below to explain how this affects the frequency.

v(wave on string) = sqrt(tension / mass per unit length)

No calculations required.
questions.expectedAnswer: As tension decreases, v decreases (from the equation). Since v = f lambda and lambda is constant (string length determines the harmonic wavelength), frequency decreases. The note played would be lower than intended.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- v or f decreased.

For Merit:
- Two points linked.

For Excellence:
- Complete answer.

questions.text:
When a 0.650 m string is played, the first harmonic has frequency 165 Hz. A finger is pressed to change the length and play a first harmonic of 220 Hz.

Calculate the new length. Assume constant tension.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:

For Merit:

For Excellence:

questions.text:
Two adjacent strings are played together. String 2 produces 110.0 Hz without a finger pressed. String 1 is gradually shortened from 0.650 m until a beat is heard.

Explain why beats form.
questions.expectedAnswer: When the two strings produce similar frequencies, the waves periodically move in and out of phase. When in phase, constructive interference produces a loud sound. When out of phase, destructive interference produces a quiet sound. This alternating loud-quiet pattern is the beat.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Constructive/destructive.

For Merit:
- Explains beat formation.

For Excellence:
- Complete answer.

questions.text: Explain what will be heard as the string length continues to be gradually reduced.
questions.expectedAnswer: As the string shortens, its frequency increases. Beat frequency = |f1 - f2|. Initially the beat frequency decreases as f1 approaches f2 = 110 Hz. When f1 = 110 Hz, no beat is heard. As string continues to shorten, f1 > 110, beat frequency increases again.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Beat decreases then increases.

For Merit:
- Explains.

For Excellence:
- Complete answer.

questions.text:
QUESTION THREE: INTERFERENCE PATTERNS

A laser shines blue light onto a double slit with separation 1.50 x 10^-4 m. Each slit acts as a coherent source. The screen is 4.00 m away, and the distance from central maxima to the 4th order maxima is 5.60 x 10^-2 m.

Show that the laser has wavelength 525 nm.
questions.expectedAnswer: sin theta approx tan theta = x/L = 0.0560/4.00 = 0.01400. n lambda = d sin theta. 4 lambda = 1.50e-4 x 0.01400. lambda = 5.25 x 10^-7 m = 525 nm.

questions.text: Explain why the intensity of light varies across the screen.
questions.expectedAnswer: When the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, waves arrive in phase (constructive interference), producing bright fringes. When the path difference is an odd number of half wavelengths, waves arrive out of phase (destructive interference), producing dark fringes. Between these extremes, intensity varies gradually.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Path difference mentioned.

For Merit:
- Constructive and destructive.

For Excellence:
- Complete answer.

questions.text:
The double slit is replaced with a diffraction grating with more closely spaced slits.

Describe and explain the changes to the interference pattern.
questions.expectedAnswer: Maxima are further apart (smaller d means larger angle for same order). Maxima are brighter (more slits contribute light). Maxima are more sharply defined (more slits means narrower peaks). Fewer maxima visible (larger angles needed for each order, some exceed 90 degrees).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- ONE change identified.

For Merit:
- ONE justified.

For Excellence:
- THREE justified.

questions.text:
In another experiment, a green laser of wavelength 525 nm is shone through a different diffraction grating and 9 maxima are seen on the screen. The screen is 1.00 m wide and 1.50 m from the grating.

Calculate the possible range of values for the slit separation.
questions.expectedAnswer: 9 maxima: 4 on each side plus central maximum. n = 4. The 4th order must fit on the screen: tan theta = 0.50/1.50, theta = 18.43 degrees. For n=4: d = n lambda/sin theta = 4 x 525e-9/sin 18.43 = 6.64e-6 m. For n=5 to NOT fit: d < 5 x 525e-9/sin 18.43 = 8.30e-6 m. So 6.64e-6 < d < 8.30e-6 m.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- n=4 or angle found.

For Merit:
- d calculated for one limit.

For Excellence:
- Both limits correct.
